subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek prefix-cache preservation: narrow heartbeat/status-only summarization, a provider-cache strategy such as the sibling PR, or broad suppression of selected tool outputs?
rationale: The code can mechanically summarize tool results, but deciding which outputs may be hidden from the model changes agent reasoning semantics and provider-cache behavior; code inspection alone should not settle that product/runtime policy.

options.title: Narrow and rebase
options.body: Restrict summarization to maintainer-approved low-value heartbeat/status results, port the change to packages/ai, and require live DeepSeek proof before closing the linked bug.

options.title: Prefer the sibling cache fix
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers choose https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95311 as the canonical provider-cache strategy and track tool-result bloat separately.

options.title: Accept broad suppression
options.body: Only proceed with the broad list if maintainers intentionally accept the reasoning risk and require focused tests plus live cache telemetry for those tools.

recommendation.title: Narrow and rebase
recommendation.body: Restrict summarization to maintainer-approved low-value heartbeat/status results, port the change to packages/ai, and require live DeepSeek proof before closing the linked bug.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mainly provider prompt-cache policy, and Vincent introduced the adjacent system prompt cache-prefix split behavior.
